title: Ensure the KDC database and master key stash are accessible only by root
description: The principal database and the stash file (.k5.<REALM>) together expose every long-term key in the realm. The audit inspects the KDC state directory (/var/lib/krb5kdc on Debian/Ubuntu, /var/kerberos/krb5kdc on RHEL) and fails if any principal* or .k5.* file has group or other permissions or is not owned by root.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - KDC database and stash file protection (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
n=0
for d in /var/lib/krb5kdc /var/kerberos/krb5kdc; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  n=$((n+1))
  bad=$(find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name 'principal*' -o -name '.k5.*' \) \( -perm /077 -o ! -user root \) 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
  [ -z "$bad" ] || { printf '%s\n' "$bad"; exit 1; }
done
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: for d in /var/lib/krb5kdc /var/kerberos/krb5kdc; do if [ -d "$d" ]; then find "$d" -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name 'principal*' -o -name '.k5.*' \) -exec chown root:root {} + -exec chmod 600 {} + || exit 1; fi; done

title: Ensure allow_weak_crypto is not enabled
description: allow_weak_crypto = true in /etc/krb5.conf re-enables single-DES and export-grade enctypes that MIT disables by default. The audit fails if the setting is true/yes/1.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Strong Kerberos encryption types (verify section number for your release)

title: Ensure kadm5.acl is owned by root and not writable by group or others
description: kadm5.acl decides which principals may administer the Kerberos database; whoever can edit it can grant themselves full kadmin rights. Checks /etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl (Debian/Ubuntu) and /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl (RHEL, default 600 root): owner root, no group or other write.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - KDC configuration file permissions (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
n=0; bad=0
for f in /etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  n=$((n+1))
  o=$(stat -Lc %U "$f") || exit 1
  [ "$o" = root ] || { echo "$f owned by $o"; bad=1; }
  [ -z "$(find -L "$f" -maxdepth 0 -perm /022)" ] || { echo "$f is group/other writable"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: for f in /etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then chown root:root "$f" && chmod 600 "$f" || exit 1; fi; done

title: Ensure the KDC does not support DES, 3DES or RC4 encryption types
description: DES and RC4-HMAC (arcfour) keys are crackable and des3-cbc-sha1 is deprecated; principals created with them weaken every ticket. The audit checks the MIT KDC configuration (/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf on Debian/Ubuntu, /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf on RHEL) and fails if supported_enctypes or master_key_type names a des, des3, rc4 or arcfour type. When unset, MIT defaults to AES only.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Strong Kerberos encryption types (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
n=0; bad=0
for f in /etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  n=$((n+1))
  grep -Eiq '^[[:space:]]*(supported_enctypes|master_key_type)[[:space:]]*=.*(des|rc4|arcfour)' "$f" && { echo "$f lists weak enctypes"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: In each [realms] entry of kdc.conf set supported_enctypes = aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96:normal aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96:normal (add aes256-cts-hmac-sha384-192:normal on 1.15+). Restart krb5kdc and kadmind, then rekey affected principals (kadmin: cpw -randkey / change password) so old DES/RC4 keys are removed; rekeying krbtgt requires planning.

title: Ensure keytab files are owned by root and accessible only by their owner
description: Keytabs contain long-term service keys usable to impersonate the service or decrypt its tickets. Checks /etc/krb5.keytab and the kadmind keytab (/etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.keytab or /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.keytab): each existing file must be owned by root with no group or other permissions.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Keytab file permissions (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
n=0; bad=0
for f in /etc/krb5.keytab /etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.keytab /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kadm5.keytab; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  n=$((n+1))
  o=$(stat -Lc %U "$f") || exit 1
  [ "$o" = root ] || { echo "$f owned by $o"; bad=1; }
  [ -z "$(find -L "$f" -maxdepth 0 -perm /077)" ] || { echo "$f is accessible by group/other"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: chown root:root <keytab> && chmod 600 <keytab> for each keytab listed. If a non-root service must read a keytab, give it a dedicated per-service keytab (ktutil) owned by that service account with mode 600 instead of opening /etc/krb5.keytab.

title: Ensure krb5.conf does not permit DES, 3DES or RC4 encryption types
description: permitted_enctypes, default_tkt_enctypes and default_tgs_enctypes in /etc/krb5.conf control which session and ticket enctypes the KDC host and its clients negotiate. The audit fails if any of them names a des, des3, rc4 or arcfour type.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Strong Kerberos encryption types (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: In [libdefaults] of /etc/krb5.conf remove weak types or set permitted_enctypes = aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96 aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96 (plus aes256-cts-hmac-sha384-192 aes128-cts-hmac-sha256-128 where supported). Verify that all clients and services have AES keys before deploying.

title: Ensure KDC and kadmind logging is configured
description: Without a [logging] section, krb5kdc and kadmind authentication and administration events may not be retained. The audit looks in kdc.conf (/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf or /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf) and /etc/krb5.conf for both "kdc =" and "admin_server =" logging destinations (FILE:, SYSLOG, STDERR, CONSOLE or DEVICE=).
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Logging (verify section number for your release)

audit.command:
files=""
for f in /etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf /etc/krb5.conf; do [ -f "$f" ] && files="$files $f"; done
[ -n "$files" ] || exit 1
lg=$(awk 'FNR==1{s=0} /^[ \t]*\[/{s=($0 ~ /^[ \t]*\[logging\]/)} s' $files)
printf '%s\n' "$lg" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*kdc[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(FILE|SYSLOG|STDERR|CONSOLE|DEVICE)' || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$lg" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*admin_server[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*(FILE|SYSLOG|STDERR|CONSOLE|DEVICE)' || exit 1
echo compliant

remediation.command: Add to kdc.conf: [logging] kdc = FILE:/var/log/krb5kdc.log  admin_server = FILE:/var/log/kadmind.log  default = SYSLOG:INFO:AUTH. Restart krb5kdc and kadmind, and include the files in log rotation and central collection.

title: Ensure maximum ticket lifetime is 10 hours or less
description: Long ticket lifetimes extend the window in which a stolen ticket can be replayed. The audit parses max_life in every realm of kdc.conf (/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf or /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf), accepting seconds, h:m[:s] and NdNhNmNs forms, and requires it to be set and at most 36000 seconds. Per-principal maximums (kadmin modprinc -maxlife) also apply and are not checked here.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Kerberos ticket lifetime (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: In each realm of kdc.conf set max_life = 10h 0m 0s, restart krb5kdc, and lower krbtgt/<REALM> with kadmin: modprinc -maxlife "10 hours" krbtgt/<REALM>.

title: Ensure maximum renewable ticket lifetime is 7 days or less
description: Renewable tickets can be refreshed without the password until max_renewable_life expires. The audit parses max_renewable_life in kdc.conf (/etc/krb5kdc/kdc.conf or /var/kerberos/krb5kdc/kdc.conf) and requires it to be set and at most 604800 seconds.
reference: CIS MIT Kerberos / Linux Benchmark guidance - Kerberos ticket lifetime (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: In each realm of kdc.conf set max_renewable_life = 7d 0h 0m 0s, restart krb5kdc, and apply the same limit to krbtgt/<REALM> with kadmin: modprinc -maxrenewlife "7 days" krbtgt/<REALM>.
